sections.heading: Overview

sections.content:
The procurement of Cane Toad Control and Surveillance services supports North Coast Local Land Services' commitment to protecting biodiversity, agricultural productivity and community wellbeing across the region. Effective control of the cane toad invasion front reduces impacts on native species, ecosystems and rural livelihoods, while supporting compliance with relevant biosecurity legislation.

This project aims to delineate and control the cane toad invasion front. The successful contractors will apply control strategies targeting all life stages of the cane toad. Control will be strategically implemented at priority high-risk pathways and invasion front sites, as determined by Local Land Services.

All control activities will be recorded, supporting consistent, data-driven decision-making. The project also strengthens community and industry capability by engaging landholders and stakeholders to increase identification and control skills, delivering long-term value through coordinated, preventative pest management across the region.
sections.heading: Project goals

sections.content:
The purpose of this procurement is to engage suitably qualified contractors to deliver cane toad control and surveillance services across identified properties within the Area of Cane Toad Activity in the North Coast region. This Request for Tender (RFT) is also intended to assist North Coast Local Land Services identify a service provider that represents overall best value for money and is fit for purpose.

The service will include the placement of trained field officers across designated areas to undertake control and surveillance targeting all life stages of cane toads, including tadpole trapping, manual hand collection, and surveillance using acoustic songmeters.

The contractor will also be required to build community and industry capacity by training landholders in cane toad identification, control, safe handling and euthanasia, and biosecurity obligations.
